summary.title: Activation of Macrophages by CpG DNA and LPS: an FTIR Spectroscopic Study
summary.authors: Emrulla Spahiu, Senol Dogan, Jörg Schnauß, Mayda Gursel, Feride Severcan
summary.executive_summary: This study investigates the global molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells upon activation with CpG DNA and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) using Attenuated Total Reflectance (ATR) Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. While CpG DNA and LPS are known to trigger innate immune responses, their impact on the relative amounts of nucleic acids, lipids, and proteins has not been previously characterized using bulk spectroscopic methods. The researchers employed ATR-FTIR to monitor cellular dynamics at 10 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, and 6 hours post-treatment. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) revealed that PC-1 accounted for 83% of the variability, guiding the selection of specific spectral peaks for detailed analysis. The results indicate that both CpG DNA and LPS treatments lead to an early increase in total nucleic acid concentration. Specifically, RNA synthesis, identified by the ribose vibration peak at 915 cm⁻¹, occurs rapidly in the first two hours, followed by DNA synthesis starting around 6 hours post-CpG stimulation. In contrast, LPS treatment primarily induced RNA synthesis without significant DNA changes, consistent with its anti-proliferative nature. Protein analysis, using Amide I and II bands, showed a rapid initial increase in total protein concentration that leveled off after two hours. Furthermore, both stimuli triggered a significant increase in fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, suggesting a shared pathway of de novo lipogenesis during macrophage activation. This study demonstrates that FTIR spectroscopy serves as a rapid, non-destructive, and independent modality to monitor the activation dynamics of macrophages, providing a holistic view of metabolic shifts that complement traditional omics techniques.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study investigates the global molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells upon activation with CpG DNA and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) using Attenuated Total Reflectance (ATR) Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. While CpG DNA and LPS are known to trigger innate immune responses, their impact on the relative amounts of nucleic acids, lipids, and proteins has not been previously characterized using bulk spectroscopic methods. The researchers employed ATR-FTIR to monitor cellular dynamics at 10 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, and 6 hours post-treatment. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) revealed that PC-1 accounted for 83% of the variability, guiding the selection of specific spectral peaks for detailed analysis. The results indicate that both CpG DNA and LPS treatments lead to an early increase in total nucleic acid concentration. Specifically, RNA synthesis, identified by the ribose vibration peak at 915 cm⁻¹, occurs rapidly in the first two hours, followed by DNA synthesis starting around 6 hours post-CpG stimulation. In contrast, LPS treatment primarily induced RNA synthesis without significant DNA changes, consistent with its anti-proliferative nature. Protein analysis, using Amide I and II bands, showed a rapid initial increase in total protein concentration that leveled off after two hours. Furthermore, both stimuli triggered a significant increase in fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, suggesting a shared pathway of de novo lipogenesis during macrophage activation. This study demonstrates that FTIR spectroscopy serves as a rapid, non-destructive, and independent modality to monitor the activation dynamics of macrophages, providing a holistic view of metabolic shifts that complement traditional omics techniques.

Research Context
FTIR spectroscopy allows non-destructive, rapid, and high-throughput analysis of biological systems. The infrared spectrum serves as a fingerprint for all metabolites of the cell system. Macrophages constitute the front line of the immune system defending the organism. CpG DNA triggers proliferation of macrophages and production of pro-inflammatory cytokines. LPS is a main constituent of the cell wall of gram-negative bacteria. How CpG ODN-mediated immune activation impacts relative amounts of metabolites has not been studied. Omics techniques require complex sample preparation steps that can alter chemical ratios. Bulk FTIR analysis provides a broad view of relative amounts of metabolites.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to monitor molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells. The cells were activated with CpG DNA and lipopolysaccharide (LPS). The hypothesis is that CpG ODN-mediated activation leads to global molecular changes. These changes are expected to be detectable by FTIR spectroscopy. The study seeks to identify sources of variation using PCA analysis. It predicts that CpG DNA and LPS increase total nucleic acid concentration. DNA synthesis is hypothesized to follow RNA synthesis in time. Both stimuli are expected to increase concentrations of fatty acids and cholesterol.

Methodological Details
Murine macrophage-like RAW 264.7 cells were cultured at 37 °C. Cells were grown in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium supplemented with 10% FBS. Cells were resuspended at a concentration of 2x10^6/mL. The control group was treated with phosphate-buffered saline (0.9% PBS). The CpG DNA group was treated with 1 µM K3 ODN. The LPS group was treated with 0.5 µg/ml LPS. Measurements were taken at 10 min, 30 min, 2 h, and 6 h. Samples were washed with sterile PBS to remove organic compounds. Infrared interferograms were collected using a Perkin-Elmer Spectrum One FTIR spectrometer. The ATR unit used a Diamond-ZnSe crystal. Spectra were recorded in the 4000-650 cm -1 region at 25°C. Cell samples of 1 µl were dried with mild N2 flux. The best signal-to-noise ratio was achieved with 128 scans. Spectral resolution was set to 2 cm -1. Replicates (n=5) were used in data analysis.

Procedures And Architectures
Post-processing included 13-point Savitzky-Golay smoothing and baseline correction. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was performed using Unscrambler 11.0 software. PCA was conducted on the 3000-650 cm -1 region. Peak assignment used center of weight measurements and literature comparison. Concentration studies were carried out by integrating curves under peaks. Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests determined the normality of datasets. Statistical analysis was performed using GraphPad Prism 8.3. The ATR surface was cleaned using a water-ethanol-water sequence.

Key Results
PC-1 gave a variability of 83% in the PCA analysis. PC-2 had a variability of 11%. CpG DNA stimulation induced significant changes in nucleic acid content from 10 min to 6 h. The RNA-specific peak at 915 cm -1 increased significantly from the first minutes. This RNA increase was maintained until 2 h after stimulation. DNA synthesis started from 6 h after stimulation with CpG DNA. LPS increased total RNA concentration up to 2 h post-stimulation. Total protein content of CpG DNA treated cells increased from 10 min to 2 h. The initial increase in protein concentration reduced starting from 2 h. There was a very significant increase in triglycerides and cholesterol from the first minutes. LPS stimulation elevated triglycerides and cholesterol concentration after 10 min. A significant increase was observed in fatty acid concentration.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The RNA-specific peak allows defining the activation state at the first minutes. LPS inhibits DNA synthesis and elicits cell cycle arrest in macrophages. The decrease in protein content may be due to secretion or oxidative stress. The increase in lipids points to de novo lipogenesis in pro-inflammatory reactions. A shared metabolite (Acetoacetyl-CoA) links fatty acid and cholesterol synthesis. FTIR spectroscopy serves as an independent modality to monitor activation dynamics. The study provides an aerial view of total protein fate.

Contradictions And Limitations
The absorbance of IR light by water is a limitation of infrared spectroscopy. The degree to which specific pathways contribute to protein loss is unknown.

Claims
FTIR spectroscopy can detect global molecular changes in macrophages upon CpG DNA and LPS activation. PCA identified sources of variation to follow with detailed spectral analysis. CpG DNA and LPS treatment increase total nucleic acid concentration. Water absorbance superimposes other signals of the aqueous cell systems. FTIR is a rapid, non-invasive tool for monitoring immune activation.
RNA synthesis precedes DNA synthesis during CpG DNA-induced macrophage activation. RNA-specific peak shows activation state in early periods. DNA synthesis starts from 6 h after stimulation. LPS does not show significant DNA changes after 6 h. This temporal sequence helps define the kinetics of immune response.
Both CpG DNA and LPS induce de novo lipogenesis in macrophages. Both activated groups increase concentration of fatty acids and cholesterol. This points to a shared synthesis pathway.  Lipid metabolism is a key component of macrophage activation.

Data And Code Availability
The protocol is available online.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
PCA was used to reduce dimensionality and draw logical conclusions. Replicates (n=5) were used to ensure statistical significance.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows PCA Scores and Loadings Plots. Figure 2 shows nucleic acid peak integrations. Figure 3 shows Amide I and II peak integrations. Figure 4 shows lipid peak integrations. Table 1 shows the study groups and treatments.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is demonstrating FTIR as a tool for monitoring macrophage activation. 2. The strongest evidence is the time-resolved increase in RNA and lipid peaks. 3. The future path involves studying mechanisms of CpG-induced protein loss.
